name: Reconstructed D1 older log dwelling #06

documented_range.note: Anonymous count-unit toward the July 1835 665-roof programme. No evidence establishes that this particular building existed, and no source names an occupant of this lot.

position.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by Randolph, Wells, Washington and Franklin; standing back from the Washington Street frontage
position.note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 5.5 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

derivation.reason: No parcel-by-parcel July 1835 roof register survives in the supplied evidence, and no lot in this block is numbered.

resident_assignment.note: NO KEEPER, AND NOT FOR WANT OF ONE (T-1685). The placement policy's platted deal seated a household on this roof under its labourer_dwellings clause, on blk_randolph_franklin#03 — a standing anonymous roof of family D1 that clause admits — and T-1685 refused to carry it onto the record: a household minted from the post office's letter lists, which the owner's ruling of 2026-08-30 (T-0379) refuses a roof: a letter-list name is a name the town knows, not a man with an address. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py --gate holds it. The placement policy's deal seated this household here anyway, and that disagreement is the deal's to answer, not this pass's to route around. The seat still stands in data/reconstruction/1835_platted_seats.json and the refusal in data/reconstruction/1835_roof_keepers.json § refused, which names the household; this note deliberately does not, because naming it here is the claim the ruling forbids. WHETHER THAT IS A SHORTAGE, MEASURED: 13 unseated household(s) of this same clause and division carry a source for their name and are refused a roof by no ruling (1835_roof_keepers.json § households_left, re-derived from the deal's own owed rows on every commit). So the roof stands empty because the deal does not consult the ruling before it deals, not because the town ran out of people. The roof itself is unchanged: a conjectural count-unit of the 665-roof programme, adopted by nobody, its existence, position and footprint as invented as before.
